summary: Interleaved keepalive heartbeats corrupt terminal boundary for >10k-token SSE responses behind corporate proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long SSE streams (typically tokenized outputs > ~10k tokens) served to their on-prem web app intermittently arrive without the terminal boundary/event (the 'done' marker) when traffic crosses their corporate HTTP/2 proxy. The stream payload itself appears intact but the final delimiter is missing or merged into a heartbeat frame, leaving the client waiting indefinitely and triggering client-side reconnects.

Impact:
- Several of FinSecure's production jobs fail to finalize in their document-generation pipeline, causing downstream ingestion to stall.
- Customer observed increased client reconnects and duplicate first-choice fragments after reconnect (not full duplication of entire transcript).

Environment:
- Customer network: corporate HTTP/2 proxy (Vendor: BlueGate) performing keepalive coalescing and aggressive connection reuse.
- Client: internal web UI using SSE polyfill + multiplexed channels for model summaries (browser-based microfrontend).
- Redwood serving path: hosted API, prod-us-west, model redwood/open-7b-v1 pinned by customer.

Observed behavior:
- Final SSE "end" event missing ~20% of the time on large outputs when proxy is in the path.
- In many cases a keepalive heartbeat chunk is interleaved at the byte boundary that would normally contain the final event metadata; client treats heartbeat as non-terminal and times out.

Expected behavior:
- For well-formed SSE streams the server should emit a clear terminal event (choice/end/done) that survives proxy traversal and is not conflated with keepalives.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer runs a long-generation request (>8k tokens) using SSE streaming via hosted API through their corporate proxy.
2) Observe stream delivery in browser console/network tab.
3) Reproduce pattern by enabling proxy keepalive/coalescing at high connection reuse (simulate with BlueGate config).
4) Repeat with smaller payloads (<1k tokens) — issue does not reproduce.

Logs and artifacts provided by customer:
- Client-side network capture (HAR): attached as FinSecure_har_2026-03-09.har
- Server request ID: req-20260309-8f3c (customer provided multiple ids; attached list)
- Short binary snapshot of last ~3KB before disconnect: attached as partial_tail_8k.bin
- Console snippets: "Waiting for final choice... no 'done' event received"

Notes on urgency:
Customer is enterprise-tier and has daily batch jobs relying on stream finalization. They triaged this as business-critical and asked for a hotfix or reliable workaround.
steps_to_reproduce: Send long SSE generation (>8k tokens) to hosted API via corporate HTTP/2 proxy that performs keepalive coalescing
Observe final event missing in browser/network tab or HAR
Disable proxy keepalive/coalescing and confirm final event consistently appears

comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged ticket, requested HAR and server-side req ids.
2026-03-10 11:40 - Customer (FinSecure): Uploaded HAR and binary tail. Said issue reproduced with BlueGate 'connection-reuse=aggressive'.
2026-03-10 15:05 - SRE (Diego Morales): Running local replay with proxy simulator; observing last event bytes sometimes sent as two frames where proxy coalesces into one control frame.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Engineering (Radhika Singh): Hypothesis: keepalive coalescing on HTTP/2 endpoint collapses SSE CRLF boundaries when frame reassembly happens; proposing guard bytes before terminal event.

investigation_notes: Reproduced with local BlueGate v2.1 simulator using 'coalesce=true' flag; final SSE event body merged with preceding keepalive and lost delimitation.
Server emits final event and 'done' metadata correctly in runtime logs; problem appears in wire/frame reassembly at proxy level.

Observed that when final event falls within same HTTP/2 DATA frame as a 1-byte keepalive marker, some proxies rewrite or drop the trailing LF resulting in client-side SSE parser not recognizing the event boundary.
Tentative fix: emit explicit 'event: done\n' header line followed by an extra LF and 4-space guard comment line prior to terminal payload to preserve boundary even if a single LF is stripped.
Alternate mitigation: add configurable stream-suffix guard in streaming runtime to always append a unique boundary token (e.g., '\\n--redwood-eof--\\n') before closing connection.
external_triage_actions: Requested BlueGate config snippet from customer: they provided 'connection_reuse=aggressive, coalesce_keepalives=true'
Opened thread in #support and pinged network-plat engineers for proxy behavior context
proposed_workarounds: 1) Customer: disable keepalive coalescing or set connection_reuse to 'moderate' on BlueGate (verified by customer reduces incidence to <1%)
2) Server-side: temporarily enable 'stream-suffix guard' feature flag in hosted path to append explicit boundary token (engineering to schedule)
resolution: In progress — short-term workaround agreed: customer will relax proxy coalescing for production batches. Engineering has a low-risk server-side change drafted to append an explicit ASCII boundary token to the end of every SSE stream; PR opened for review and small canary planned in prod-us-west.
next_steps: Engineering to land PR that appends explicit end-of-stream guard token (refer to PR #964)
Run canary on 2% of traffic in prod-us-west and monitor for missing terminal events (metric: sse_missing_terminal_event)
If canary passes, roll out to 20% then 100% and notify FinSecure well before full rollout
SRE to coordinate with customer to temporarily alter BlueGate config for urgent batches
root_cause: Frame coalescing behavior in certain HTTP/2 proxies can collapse SSE event delimiters when keepalive markers are coalesced into adjacent data frames; this causes the client SSE parser to miss the terminal event if a trailing LF is stripped by proxy rewrite.
